scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, chemical composition, mechanical properties, dimensional tolerances, and testing schedules for copper wires used for general and industrial engineering purposes. It covers wires with cross-sectional diameters ranging from 0.50 mm up to and including 6.00 mm, supplied in either the annealed (soft) or hard-drawn condition.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Copper Products (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all copper wires for general engineering purposes must conform to IS 4412:1981 and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Medium and large-scale enterprises had to comply by October 19, 2024, small enterprises by January 19, 2025, and micro enterprises by April 19, 2025. Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified copper engineering wires in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Exemption is granted solely for export-oriented shipments. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial copper wire feedstocks.

requirements.detail: Every coil or packaged bundle of copper wire must carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 4412) printed on a secure tag or label.

The wire must be manufactured from electrolytically or fire-refined copper, conforming to the chemical composition limits of Grade Cu-ETP (Electrolytic Tough Pitch) or Cu-FRHC (Fire Refined High Conductivity) as specified in IS 191. Copper purity must be a minimum of 99.90 percent (including silver).

Copper wire is supplied as specified by the purchaser in one of two distinct conditions: a) O — Annealed (soft) [usually for woven mesh or flexible ties]; b) HD — Hard (hard-drawn) [usually for high structural strength applications].
The standard specifies requirements for wire diameters ranging from 0.50 mm to 6.00 mm, with rationalized sizes and tight manufacturing tolerances to ensure uniform cross-section.
The wire surface must be clean, smooth, bright, and completely free from physical defects such as cracks, severe scratches, oxidation scale, flakes, draw marks, or foreign inclusions.

When required by the purchaser to verify material resistance against cracking during high-temperature heat-treatment, welding, or brazing under reducing atmospheres, specimens must pass the Hydrogen Embrittlement test. Samples heated in a hydrogen atmosphere at 900°C must show zero microscopic or macroscopic cracking or surface blistering.

requirements.requirement_type: Audit Sampling Scale and Guidelines (Product Manual)

requirements.detail: All copper wires of the same size, shape, condition, and manufactured through the same process from the same cast/heat of raw material constitute one control unit. One random sample is tested per heat/cast for chemical composition, and one sample per control unit for tensile and physical properties.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 4412 : 1981 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing copper wires (diameters from 0.50 mm to 6.00 mm) designed for general and industrial engineering purposes—including structural components, general hardware, mechanical fasteners, and wire mesh grids. Under India's statutory Copper Products Quality Control Order (QCO), all copper engineering wires supplied, sold, or imported domestically must conform to this standard and bear the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to ensure uniform quality and material purity. Wires are woven or drawn from high-purity copper (minimum 99.90% purity) and classified into annealed (soft) and hard-drawn tempers. The standard enforces detailed chemical, dimensional, and mechanical limits—including strict diameter tolerances, minimum tensile strength, high elongation (up to 40% for annealed wire), and an optional high-temperature hydrogen embrittlement test to verify jointing integrity.
